sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: NPS L59 explicitly distinguishes signs allowing walking from zones closed to all entry; L28/L31 directs reading/following the on-site sign. The actual prompt states a bird-nesting area closed by an entry-ban sign, not just a vehicle restriction. Only key3 stays outside; quiet, unseen-nest and quick/no-photo choices still enter. The separate L32 tideline pass-through and L33 turtle pedestrian rules are not this stated case.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Нужно выбрать путь за пределами участка, закрытого для входа. NPS просит следовать знакам: беспокойство может заставить взрослых птиц покинуть гнёзда.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: Sentence1 selects an outside route for the all-entry ban, consistent with L59. Sentence2 combines obey-sign direction L28/L31/L59 with L40’s possibility of nest abandonment due to human activity. It asserts neither inevitable abandonment nor a ban across every protection zone.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Даже присутствие людей может заставить взрослых птиц покинуть гнёзда.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: NPS L40 says human activity can cause adults to abandon nests. The note correctly describes possible disturbance from human presence, not just loud noise; moving quietly does not create permission to enter. No guaranteed effect on every nest is asserted.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Гнёзда береговых птиц трудно заметить и обойти.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: NPS L40 says shorebird nests are very difficult to see and avoid. That is a concrete visibility fact about the option relying on unseen nests; failure to see them cannot establish harmless or permitted crossing.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Если знак запрещает любой вход, проход пешком через эту зону тоже запрещён.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: NPS L59 explicitly distinguishes walking-permitted zones from areas closed to all entry. In the latter, fast pedestrian passage is still entry, so no-photo/no-stopping is not an exception. The conditional note preserves the real difference from L32 tideline pass-through and L33 vehicle-only turtle restrictions.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: При опасности птенцы замирают и сливаются с песком, поэтому их легко не заметить.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: NPS L40 directly states threatened young chicks hide by staying perfectly still and blending with sand. The note retains this protective behavior and its immediate visibility implication. This is additional chick behavior beyond the whole prompt/key signed-closure route choice, and not merely repetition of the no-entry rule.

absoluteLevel.ground: Broad adult protected-visitor judgment: obey an explicit entry ban and choose an outside route. Cape Lookout supplies setting, not an obscure geographic clue; no species identification, season date, buffer measurement or legal recall is needed. Wrong choices are real visitor rationalizations (quiet, unseen nests, quick non-stopping passage), not absurd entities; the source itself shows why actual sign distinctions matter.

correctNoteExtraFact.fact: Threatened chicks remain still and blend with the sand, making them easy to overlook.
correctNoteExtraFact.beyondWholePromptAndKey: The whole question/key gives a signed closed nesting area and outside route; it does not describe chick defensive behavior or camouflage. The note adds a concrete fact about the protected young birds themselves.

taxonomy.ground: Protected-natural-shore access management for nesting wildlife at an actual national seashore. The MAIN is conservation-zone entry compliance, not a general urban sign or abstract ecological theory.
